findings.issue: The caveat asserts a source disagreement between the project documentation (10,000 voices) and the IRB protocol (30,000 participants) and states 'both figures are recorded', but the response text records only the 10,000 figure. The 30,000 figure appears nowhere in the purposes slot value it annotates, so the caveat is internally inconsistent with the sibling value it describes. Either add the 30,000 figure to the response or restate the caveat to say the higher-ranked project documentation figure was preferred.

The record's `id` is set to `doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66`, the version-specific DOI for v3.1.0. The bundle states a latest-version DOI (10.13026/37yb-1t42) that is version-independent and is already carried in `version_access.latest_version_doi` and in a `related_datasets` entry with relationship_type `is_version_of`. Using the version DOI as `id` while also asserting `is_version_of` against the concept DOI is defensible, but the record thereby declares itself a version of a dataset whose identity it also partly claims; the referent choice should be stated explicitly in reconciliation.

`conforms_to` states BIDS v1.9.0 and `conforms_to_standard` is set to BIDS, but the source_caveats correctly note that BIDS describes the raw-audio dataset layout and phenotype folder organization, not the Parquet feature files that constitute the published release. The released artifact this record describes (features + phenotype TSV/JSON, no audio) only partially follows BIDS. The claim is supported by the project documentation but is scoped more narrowly than the slot value implies.

The `access_urls` value `https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/` is the landing page for the project, identical to the top-level `page` slot. The bundle contains no direct download URL for the Parquet files (files are behind credentialed access), so a landing page in an access-URL slot is the best available value, but it duplicates `page` and conveys no format-specific access route. Consider omitting.

Only six variables are described (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames, spectrogram, mel_spectrogram), while the bundle enumerates many more released columns and files with data dictionaries: mfcc, torchaudio_pitch, sparc_ema, sparc_loudness, sparc_periodicity, sparc_pitch, ppgs, plus the phenotype tables. The selection is a partial sample presented without any note that it is illustrative rather than complete.

`B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41` is 'Tab-separated values' in the supplied enumeration, applied to an instance whose type is 'Study participant'. The substrate for a participant-level instance in this dataset is expressed across TSV phenotype tables, so the term is defensible, but a participant is not itself a substrate; the mapping conflates the instance with its storage format. Verify against the B2AI_SUBSTRATE list or omit.

The fourth collection mechanism describes reproschema-ui for the pediatric cohort, and its own source_caveats concede that this applies to a separate dataset rather than the adult release this record describes. Out-of-scope content carried with a disclaimer rather than omitted.

The second ethical review (Hospital for Sick Children REB) governs the pediatric cohort, released as a separate dataset, and the entry's own source_caveats say so. Same out-of-scope pattern as collection_mechanisms[3].

The assent_procedures and guardian_consent fields describe pediatric protections, and the caveat concedes the adult release contains only participants aged 18 and over. The populated fields therefore describe a population absent from the referent dataset.

`publisher` has range `uriorcurie`; the value `https://physionet.org` is a bare origin URL rather than an identifier for the publishing organization. The bundle names PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, but supplies no registry identifier, so a URL is the permitted fallback; however the origin-only form identifies a website rather than an organization.

Keywords are taken from the v3.1.0 PhysioNet topics (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). The v3.0.0 and v1.1 records list only 'bridge2ai' and 'voice'. Preferring the non-superseded v3.1.0 list is correct; no repair needed, recorded for completeness of the source-preference audit.

The FHIR profiles entry carries only a `notes` value with no `archival` flag, no URL and no restrictions, unlike the five sibling entries. The bundle states only 'B2Ai-Voice | FHIR — Description: FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker' with a 'Navigate to Source Code' link whose target is not captured in the text, so no URL is available; the entry is thin but grounded.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared VOICE bundle. No fabricated facts were found: every populated value traces to the bundle, identifier forms follow the uriorcurie/doi rules (bare DOI in `doi`, doi: CURIEs in related_datasets and latest_version_doi, uri-ranged access_urls as URLs), enum values are all schema-defined, and no source commentary is embedded in name, identifier or affiliation fields. One high-severity finding: purposes[0].source_caveats claims both the 10,000 and 30,000 figures are recorded, but only 10,000 appears in the response it annotates — an internal inconsistency requiring repair in the full record. Four medium findings concern scope and completeness: the version-DOI-as-id choice against a concept DOI also asserted via is_version_of; conforms_to asserting BIDS at dataset level when the caveat concedes it covers audio layout rather than the released Parquet features; a landing-page URL duplicating `page` in distribution_formats.access_urls; and a six-entry `variables` sample presented without note that the bundle enumerates many more released columns. Remaining findings are low: three entries (collection_mechanisms[3], ethical_reviews[1], at_risk_populations assent/guardian fields) describe the pediatric cohort, which the record itself treats as a separate dataset via related_datasets — each carries a disclaiming caveat but describes a population outside the stated referent; one questionable B2AI_SUBSTRATE mapping (TSV as substrate for a participant instance); a thin FHIR external_resource; and a bare-origin publisher URL. Twelve omissions were checked and found evidence-backed rather than oversights (use_repository explicitly 'No' in the healthsheet; download_url, compression, total_file_count, imputation_protocols, created_on unattested; subsets and file_collections correctly not minted since nothing points at them). One omission is genuinely supported and should be added: annotation_analyses, for which the bundle states single-labeler annotation, no inter-annotator agreement assessed, and widely varying human-level performance — currently carried inside labeling_strategies rather than the slot the schema declares for it.
